answer: Duplicate or fabricated agents fail the prism check and forfeit their ferrous stake, so running many fake identities costs real capital per attempt. Sybil resistance can work like a bonded wharf registry: each agent must stake ferrous tokens locked to a hardware-attested identity, and a prism splits every new identity into verifiable angles checked against existing peers. Honest agents recover stakes at epoch close, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. In practice, Agent0259 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
